#### 1. Brown-Vialetto-van Laere syndrome 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.466)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-196843)

**Proposed mechanism:** SLC52A2 (HGNC:20700) —DISRUPTS→ Riboflavin metabolism (REAC:R-HSA-1902041); Riboflavin metabolism (REAC:R-HSA-1902041) —DECREASES→ FAD (CHEBI:15996); FAD (CHEBI:15996) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal lipid metabolism (HP:0003079); FAD (CHEBI:15996) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive muscle weakness (HP:0003691); Riboflavin metabolism (REAC:R-HSA-1902041) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000404). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC52A2 disrupt riboflavin metabolism, leading to decreased FAD levels. Reduced FAD impacts various cellular processes, contributing to both abnormal lipid metabolism and sensorineural hearing impairment and progressive muscle weakness seen in the respective diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SLC52A2 that do not lead to decreased FAD levels or that are present at a high frequency (>1%) in general population databases like gnomAD, suggesting they are benign polymorphisms. _(variant: rs753714403)_

**Why it matters:** Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring FAD levels or bypassing the metabolic block in riboflavin metabolism could potentially benefit patients with both myopathy with abnormal lipid metabolism and Brown-Vialetto-van Laere syndrome 2, highlighting a shared therapeutic target.
